newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Protestors block soya shipment to Antwerp port.
newsitem.headline: Protestors block soya shipment to Antwerp port.

text.p: Greenpeace environmentalists stepped up their protest against genetically altered soybeans Thursday by stopping a Polish bulk carrier it believed had the beans on board from docking at the Belgian port of Antwerp.
Inflatable dinghies blocked the ship in a lock on the approach to the port, and four activists chained themselves to a drawbridge at the port entrance to prevent it opening.
Protesters had hung a banner reading "genetic experiment - don't buy it," though the atmosphere at the scene remained calm.

In a statement, Greenpeace said the Polish-registerd Ziemia Zamojska was carrying a U.S. grain shipment that left Cleveland, Ohio, on Oct. 8, and that Greenpeace had stopped it from unloading in Antwerp at the wharf of U.S. grain multinational Cargill.
It said the ship was believed to be carrying the new type of bean which has been developed by U.S. chemicals group Monsanto to be resistant to its own new "super weedkiller" Roundup.
